 Mercedes' $10 million gamble on an F1 prodigy who doesn't even have a driver's license.
 Mercedes is investing $10 million and betting on Kimi Antonelli, a 2006-born driver who doesn't yet have a license, to succeed F1 superstar Lewis Hamilton after his departure in December 2024.
 ZNews • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 
 Despite not having a street driving license, Kimi Antonelli was given a spot in Mercedes' Formula 1 racing team at the age of 11. Photo: Timmy Huynh/WSJ .
 When Lewis Hamilton left Mercedes in December 2024, the F1 team had a plethora of top-tier options worldwide . However, they handed the seven-time champion's seat to Kimi Antonelli (born in 2006), a teenager who at the time didn't even have a street driver's license.
 However, behind that bold decision were seven years of training, thousands of hours of preparation, and a $10 million investment, the WSJ reported.
 Mercedes discovered Antonelli after witnessing the talent of the go-kart prodigy from Bologna, Italy. Kimi is expected to pass his racing license test at the end of January 2025, approximately six weeks before the first F1 race in Australia in March 2025.
 Two years after his appointment, Mercedes' investment is poised to yield significant results. At 20 years old, Antonelli could become the youngest F1 champion in history if favorable results are achieved this weekend in Austin, USA. While he may not be crowned champion immediately, he still has a chance to break Sebastian Vettel's record, who won the world championship at the age of 23. 
 Ever since discovering Antonelli as an 11-year-old go-kart racing prodigy, Mercedes has been training him. Photo: Paul Ripke/Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited. 
 A multi-million dollar gamble on young talent.
 Even in the rigorous selection environment of elite sports , discovering a potential F1 champion in elementary school is still a risky decision. Few people can look at a 32kg boy and imagine that this teenager is capable of handling a nearly 1,000-horsepower F1 engine.
 Toto Wolff, CEO of the Mercedes racing team, is one of them.
 "Even from a very young age, you can tell if a child has exceptional talent," Wolff said. According to him, the ability to control the car in the rain, reflexes, and courage at high speeds are important indicators of a young F1 driver's potential.
 While Ferrari considered Antonelli too young and small, Wolff saw an opportunity in the boy's go-kart racing skills. He decided to invest in a talent who lacked extensive experience at the highest level.
 This is no cheap gamble. A go-kart racing season can cost a driver's family over $200,000 . Therefore, when bringing a young athlete into their training program, F1 teams usually only select a select few they trust.
 Mercedes then had six drivers aged 11 to 17 in their development program. With Antonelli, the team covered all expenses, from karting competitions, physical training, nutrition, and equipment to lower-level Formula One races.
 "We cover travel expenses, hire fitness and nutrition coaches, buy racing shoes, protective gear, gloves, and helmets. You just focus on driving," Wolff said.
 You may also like This support came with expectations of success. Antonelli successively proved himself worthy of the investment, thereby convincing Mercedes to continue investing. 
 Antonelli was brought to the 2018 Monaco Grand Prix by Toto Wolff. Photo: Paul Ripke/Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited. 
 The journey behind the F1 driver's seat.
 Mercedes not only helped Antonelli improve his skills on the racetrack, but also prepared him for other requirements of an F1 driver, from media communication and personal image building to fluency in English. This is a crucial language for communication between the driver, engineers, and the tactical team.
 Antonelli was also taken to Grand Prix races to observe how an F1 team operates. These experiences helped him get acquainted with the professional racing environment early on, instead of having to get used to everything when he officially debuted.
 "No other 16-year-old has had the opportunity to witness what goes on inside a Formula 1 team like he did," Wolff said.
 In the spring of 2024, Antonelli tested his F1 car for the first time in a closed-door session in Austria, under harsh weather conditions. His ability to drive in the rain had previously impressed Mercedes drivers, but this time, he faced snow and the pressure of dozens of engineers and mechanics monitoring every lap.
 According to those present, Antonelli was surprised and asked if all those people had really come just to serve his experiment.
 A few months later, he won his first Formula 2 (F2) race, the sub-F1 series. Mercedes decided to replace Hamilton with the young driver and announced the selection that summer . Antonelli's annual compensation package was reportedly around $2 million .
 Andrew Shovlin, Mercedes' Chief Race Officer, admitted the team had initially worried that the amount of knowledge to be imparted might exceed the capacity of a young driver. However, early preparation helped Antonelli quickly adapt to the cockpit and technical requirements. 
 Antonelli's first F1 test in spring 2024 in Austria. Photo: Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited. 
 A tough rookie season.
 Despite his great potential, Antonelli still faced the typical challenges of a first F1 season. The Mercedes car wasn't strong enough to compete for the championship, while the team prioritized development for the 2026 season, when major changes to the technical regulations would significantly impact how the car operates.
 Mercedes expects Antonelli's youth, hundreds of hours of training on simulators, and quick learning ability to help him adapt. His initial goal is to gain experience, minimize mistakes, and prepare for future F1 seasons.
 You may also like Wolff doesn't expect his protégé to avoid every setback. He predicts the first season will have both brilliant moments and disappointing mistakes. The important thing is that Mercedes continues to be patient with its choices.
 Antonelli finished fourth in his Australian debut race in March 2025, but subsequently experienced a slump, failing to score points in six out of seven races. At the Belgian Grand Prix at the end of July 2025, he broke down in tears in front of the media after being disappointed with the qualifying results.
 Such moments challenge both the driver and the confidence of the development team. However, Mercedes remains committed to its long-term plan, while Antonelli continues to gain experience and improve his performance in F1.
 For Wolff, the decision to invest in Antonelli was not only based on his immediate achievements, but also stemmed from a belief in the young rider's natural talent.
 "There are children who are born to be excellent racers. He is one of them," he said.
